hero.title: A real console. A fuller shell. Independent providers.
hero.lede: Dekopon 0.11 adds an interactive terminal console, a substantially more capable sandboxed shell, a public provider testkit, and cleaner separation between the core platform and independently released providers. Version 0.11.1 repairs the container runtime base without changing crate behavior.

summary: The core rule is unchanged: models propose and the broker authorizes. The new console makes that boundary visible while you work, and the richer shell gives models more room to plan inside it.

highlights.title: Watch one agent session without moving authority into the CLI.
highlights.body: A bare dekopon command on a terminal opens a TUI over the running broker. It shows the selected agent, effective capabilities, scripts, inputs, and results while keeping its local execution leg empty.
points: Attested local development subjects are explicit and off by default
Every capability still reaches the separate broker
Render-time control stripping and field-level secret redaction

highlights.title: Use more real shell habits without launching a host process.
highlights.body: The homemade interpreter now supports defensive options, richer parameter expansion, compound pipelines, read, getopts, double brackets, and script-addressable output streams.
points: if, loops, case, groups, functions, and redirections compose
No host files, inherited environment, subprocesses, or ambient sockets

highlights.title: Test and release integrations outside the core repository.
highlights.body: The public testkit runs a component against the real storage host. GitHub moved to its own repository, and a SQLite-compatible Turso provider now ships independently.
points: FakeBroker for end-to-end provider storage tests
GitHub component with nineteen narrow capabilities
Independent provider tags, assets, checksums, and provenance

path.title: See the request. Keep the decision elsewhere.
path.body: The console observes the same agent loop used by chat. It can display proposals and results, but it links no policy, provider credential store, or provider host.
path.ariaLabel: How one Dekopon console turn reaches the separate broker

changes.title: The operator gets an interactive view over a live broker session.
changes.body: The TUI shows declared and effectively granted capabilities, then folds each turn’s scripts and broker calls. Observation decorators cannot influence the session, and the CLI retains no local provider execution path.

changes.title: Common defensive and compositional shell patterns now work.
changes.body: Models can use read-shaped loops, getopts, double brackets, real errexit and nounset behavior, pipefail, richer parameter expansion, grouped pipeline stages, and bounded in-memory redirection.

changes.title: Storage-backed providers can test against the real host without standing up Cedar.
changes.body: dekopon-provider-sdk-testkit mints test authorization and exercises the production StorageHost over a temporary root. It is a provider-development harness, not runtime authority.

changes.title: GitHub and SQL move at their own release cadence.
changes.body: The GitHub component left the core tree with its PR-review walkthrough. Turso SQL adds SQLite-compatible durable storage through the existing exact storage interface. Nothing in core depends on either component.

changes.title: The console no longer borrows an identifier that looks externally authenticated.
changes.body: The new dev.<surface>.<name> subject family is admitted only when the broker explicitly enables development subjects. It still maps through owner-controlled identity and Cedar policy.

changes.title: The published image now matches the glibc required by the release binaries.
changes.body: Version 0.11.0’s image publish failed because the console binary named weak glibc 2.39 symbols while the Debian 12 runtime carried glibc 2.36. Version 0.11.1 moves the image to Debian 13; crate source is unchanged.

detailsIntro: The console, shell, provider testkit, and independently shipped integrations keep the same proposal, policy, constraint, execution, and evidence path. The patch release changes only image compatibility.

telemetry.title: authority moved to the console, gateway, or model
telemetry.body: The console holds a model credential and observes one agent loop. Cedar, execution constraints, provider credentials, provider execution, replay protection, and durable audit remain inside the separate broker.
telemetry.note: The current local deployment still treats one Unix UID as a trust domain. Dekopon remains pre-production.

packages.name: Homebrew
packages.body: The generated formula is verified against the current published archives and installs all four executables.

packages.name: crates.io
packages.body: All 25 public workspace crates, including the TUI and provider testkit, are published at the current application version.

packages.name: Container
packages.body: The Debian 13 distroless multi-architecture image is published for the broker, gateway, runner, or operator CLI.

installIntro: The application release is available through Homebrew, crates.io, attested GitHub archives, and the multi-architecture image. The latest published Helm chart remains 0.2.0 with application 0.10.0; chart 0.2.1 is present in source but not published.

current: Interactive terminal console over one broker-authorized agent session
A broader bash-shaped language with no operating-system shell
Public provider SDK testkit backed by the real storage host
Twenty-five public crates published at the current application version
Independent GitHub, MediaWiki, Python, ripgrep, and Turso SQL provider releases
A published multi-architecture container image for the current release

scopeIntro: The full local path includes gateway or console attestation, Cedar, broker-managed credentials, Wasm providers, audit, and telemetry. Stronger process isolation and audit anchoring remain.
